quickviz trigger boundary

The gap this closes

CI eval job, before:

  Skill:     quickviz
  Trigger:   N/A  (not measured: the spec declares no trigger cases)

Why it matters now. This PR series rewrote quickviz’s entire usage model — from “give it a self-contained topic” to “render the current conversation”. Activation was unverified in exactly the place it changed most.

The phrasing is deliberately scrappy. The replay showed this skill is asked for as a modifier on an existing question, never as a standalone topic — polished test prompts would have encoded a user who does not exist.

Negatives — where the real value is

This is the collision the brainstorm predicted. It killed the “add a new quickviz skill alongside ascii-visualizer” option precisely because two near-identical descriptions create routing ambiguity. quickviz now sits next to visualize-plan, separated only by whether the deliverable is an inline reply or a file. These three cases make that boundary testable instead of assumed.

The last row is the honest one. Executing trigger cases means paid LLM calls through the CI eval job — the same job currently returning INCONCLUSIVE on a harness outage, and the same spend the operator’s standing rule says never to incur locally without consent. These cases are declared and schema-valid; whether the skill actually fires on them is measured by CI, not by this PR.
